import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The $\frac 1 3$–$\frac 2 3$ conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1/3%E2%80%932/3_conjecture)
-/

namespace Conjecture_1_3_to_2_3

/--
Does every finite partially ordered set that is not totally ordered
contain two elements $x$ and $y$ such that the probability that
$x$ appears before $y$ in a random linear extension is between $\frac 1 3$ and $\frac 2 3$?

The set of all total order extensions is represented as order preserving
bijections $P$ of $1, ..., n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 6]
theorem conjecture_1_3_to_2_3 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (P : Type) [Finite P] [PartialOrder P]
    (not_total : ¬ Std.Total (α := P) (· ≤ ·)) (total_ext : Set <| OrderHom P ℕ)
    (total_ext_def : ∀ σ, σ ∈ total_ext ↔ Set.range σ = Set.Icc 1 (Nat.card P)),
    ∃ x y : P, ({σ ∈ total_ext | σ x < σ y}.ncard / total_ext.ncard : ℚ)
      ∈ Set.Icc (1/3) (2/3) := by
  sorry

end Conjecture_1_3_to_2_3

reformulations.difference: Linear extensions are represented by monotone maps P → ℕ whose range is exactly {1,…,|P|}, without a separate injectivity hypothesis. The extension set is universally quantified and characterized by a membership equivalence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite P of cardinality n, the interval {1,…,n} also has cardinality n. Surjectivity onto that interval therefore forces injectivity. Such monotone bijective rank maps correspond one-to-one to total orders extending P, and σ x < σ y means exactly that x precedes y. The membership equivalence uniquely determines the set of all these maps. Scratch proofs establish the range-condition ↔ Set.BijOn equivalence, equivalence of the full quantified RHS with the canonical explicit-bijection formulation, and finiteness and nonemptiness of the extension set. Consequently, the ncard quotient is precisely the uniform probability in the source.

sources_consulted: Ashwin Sah, Improving the 1/3–2/3 Conjecture for Width Two Posets, arXiv:1811.01500v2, Introduction and §5.2; LaTeX source downloaded from https://arxiv.org/e-print/1811.01500
review.notes: Checked the sole theorem against Wikipedia and Sah's precise statement. The inclusive bounds, non-totality restriction, and answer scope agree; Wikipedia explicitly says the general conjecture remains unsolved. Lean inspection confirms that both cardinalities are cast before rational division. Empty and singleton posets are excluded by non-totality, and equal witnesses cannot meet the lower bound. Tests cover small chains and antichains, a direct proof of the original quotient being 1/2 for a two-element antichain, and the three-element source example attaining 1/3 and 2/3. All final experiments compile in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the verification proofs do not depend on sorryAx.
